sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca svargaṃ triviṣṭapaṃ prāpya mama pūrvapitāmahāḥ pāṇḍavā dhārtarāṣṭrāś ca kāni sthānāni bhejire
english: Janamejaya said: Having reached heaven, the threefold celestial realm, what abodes did my forefathers attain—the Pāṇḍavas and the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra alike?

sanskrit: etad icchāmy ahaṃ śrotuṃ sarvavic cāsi me mataḥ maharṣiṇābhyanujñāto vyāsenādbhutakarmaṇā
english: This I wish to hear, for I hold you to be one who knows all things, sanctioned as you are by the great sage Vyāsa of wondrous deeds.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca svargaṃ triviṣṭapaṃ prāpya tava pūrvapitāmahāḥ yudhiṣṭhiraprabhṛtayo yad akurvata tac chṛṇu
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Hear, then, what your forefathers did—Yudhiṣṭhira and the rest—once they had reached heaven, the threefold celestial realm.

sanskrit: svargaṃ triviṣṭapaṃ prāpya dharmarājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ duryodhanaṃ śriyā juṣṭaṃ dadarśāsīnam āsane
english: Having reached heaven, the threefold celestial realm, the Dharma-king Yudhiṣṭhira beheld Duryodhana seated upon a throne, attended by splendor.

sanskrit: bhrājamānam ivādityaṃ vīralakṣmyābhisaṃvṛtam devair bhrājiṣṇubhiḥ sādhyaiḥ sahitaṃ puṇyakarmabhiḥ
english: Blazing like the sun, encompassed by the glory of heroes, surrounded by the radiant gods and the Sādhyas of holy deeds.

sanskrit: tato yudhiṣṭhiro dṛṣṭvā duryodhanam amarṣitaḥ sahasā saṃnivṛtto 'bhūc chriyaṃ dṛṣṭvā suyodhane
english: Then Yudhiṣṭhira, seeing Duryodhana, grew indignant, and at once turned back when he beheld such splendor upon Suyodhana.

sanskrit: bruvann uccair vacas tān vai nāhaṃ duryodhanena vai sahitaḥ kāmaye lokāṃl lubdhenādīrghadarśinā
english: Speaking aloud to them, he said: I have no wish to share these worlds in the company of Duryodhana, that greedy and short-sighted man.

sanskrit: yatkṛte pṛthivī sarvā suhṛdo bāndhavās tathā hatāsmābhiḥ prasahyājau kliṣṭaiḥ pūrvaṃ mahāvane
english: For whose sake the whole earth, and our friends and kinsmen too, were slain by us in furious battle—we who had first been tormented in the great forest.

sanskrit: draupadī ca sabhāmadhye pāñcālī dharmacāriṇī parikliṣṭānavadyāṅgī patnī no gurusaṃnidhau
english: And Draupadī, the Pāñcāla princess, devoted to righteousness, our blameless-limbed wife, was sorely abused in the midst of the assembly, in the presence of our elders.

sanskrit: svasti devā na me kāmaḥ suyodhanam udīkṣitum tatrāhaṃ gantum icchāmi yatra te bhrātaro mama
english: Farewell, O gods! I have no desire to look upon Suyodhana. I wish to go to where my brothers are.

sanskrit: maivam ity abravīt taṃ tu nāradaḥ prahasann iva svarge nivāso rājendra viruddhaṃ cāpi naśyati
english: Not so, said Nārada to him, smiling as it were: In heaven, O lord of kings, where one dwells, all enmity perishes.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira mahābāho maivaṃ vocaḥ kathaṃ cana duryodhanaṃ prati nṛpaṃ śṛṇu cedaṃ vaco mama
english: Mighty-armed Yudhiṣṭhira, speak not so by any means concerning King Duryodhana; and hear these words of mine.

sanskrit: eṣa duryodhano rājā pūjyate tridaśaiḥ saha sadbhiś ca rājapravarair ya ime svargavāsinaḥ
english: This King Duryodhana is honored together with the thirty gods and with those virtuous, foremost kings who dwell here in heaven.

sanskrit: vīralokagatiṃ prāpto yuddhe hutvātmanas tanum yūyaṃ sarve surasamā yena yuddhe samāsitāḥ
english: He has attained the realm of heroes, having offered up his own body in battle—that battle in which all of you, godlike men, were arrayed against him.

sanskrit: sa eṣa kṣatradharmeṇa sthānam etad avāptavān bhaye mahati yo 'bhīto babhūva pṛthivīpatiḥ
english: By the law of the warrior he has won this station, this lord of the earth who remained fearless in the midst of great peril.

sanskrit: na tan manasi kartavyaṃ putra yad dyūtakāritam draupadyāś ca parikleśaṃ na cintayatum arhasi
english: You must not take to heart, my son, what was brought about by the dicing; nor ought you to dwell upon the abuse of Draupadī.

sanskrit: ye cānye 'pi parikleśā yuṣmākaṃ dyūtakāritāḥ saṃgrāmeṣv atha vānyatra na tān saṃsmartum arhasi
english: And whatever other torments were inflicted upon you through the dicing, whether in battles or elsewhere, you ought not to recall them.

sanskrit: samāgaccha yathānyāyaṃ rājñā duryodhanena vai svargo 'yaṃ neha vairāṇi bhavanti manujādhipa
english: Meet King Duryodhana in due courtesy. This is heaven, O lord of men; here no enmities exist.

sanskrit: nāradenaivam uktas tu kururājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ bhrātṝn papraccha medhāvī vākyam etad uvāca ha
english: Thus addressed by Nārada, the Kuru king Yudhiṣṭhira, wise as he was, asked after his brothers and spoke these words.

sanskrit: yadi duryodhanasyaite vīralokāḥ sanātanāḥ adharmajñasya pāpasya pṛthivīsuhṛdadruhaḥ
english: If these are the eternal worlds of heroes for Duryodhana—a wicked man, ignorant of righteousness, a betrayer of the earth and of his friends—

sanskrit: yatkṛte pṛthivī naṣṭā sahayā sarathadvipā vayaṃ ca manyunā dagdhā vairaṃ praticikīrṣavaḥ
english: for whose sake the earth was laid waste with its horses, chariots, and elephants, and we ourselves were burned by wrath, seeking to repay our feud—

sanskrit: ye te vīrā mahātmāno bhrātaro me mahāvratāḥ satyapratijñā lokasya śūrā vai satyavādinaḥ
english: then where are those heroes, those great-souled brothers of mine, men of mighty vows, true to their pledges, the world's brave and truthful champions?

sanskrit: teṣām idānīṃ ke lokā draṣṭum icchāmi tān aham karṇaṃ caiva mahātmānaṃ kaunteyaṃ satyasaṃgaram
english: What worlds are theirs now? I wish to behold them—and the great-souled Karṇa, the son of Kuntī, true to his battle-pledge.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnaṃ sātyakiṃ ca dhṛṣṭadyumnasya cātmajān ye ca śastrair vadhaṃ prāptāḥ kṣatradharmeṇa pārthivāḥ
english: Dhṛṣṭadyumna and Sātyaki, and the sons of Dhṛṣṭadyumna, and those kings who met their death by weapons according to the warrior's law.

sanskrit: kva nu te pārthivā brahman naitān paśyāmi nārada virāṭadrupadau caiva dhṛṣṭaketumukhāṃś ca tān
english: Where then are those kings, O brāhmaṇa? I do not see them here, Nārada—Virāṭa and Drupada, and those led by Dhṛṣṭaketu.

sanskrit: śikhaṇḍinaṃ ca pāñcālyaṃ draupadeyāṃś ca sarvaśaḥ abhimanyuṃ ca durdharṣaṃ draṣṭum icchāmi nārada
english: And Śikhaṇḍin the Pāñcāla, and all the sons of Draupadī, and the unassailable Abhimanyu—these I wish to behold, Nārada.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca neha paśyāmi vibudhā rādheyam amitaujasam bhrātarau ca mahātmānau yudhāmanyūttamaujasau
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Here, O gods, I do not see Rādheya of measureless might, nor the two great-souled brothers Yudhāmanyu and Uttamaujas.

sanskrit: juhuvur ye śarīrāṇi raṇavahnau mahārathāḥ rājāno rājaputrāś ca ye madarthe hatā raṇe
english: those great warriors who offered their bodies into the fire of battle—the kings and princes who were slain in war for my sake.

sanskrit: kva te mahārathāḥ sarve śārdūlasamavikramāḥ tair apy ayaṃ jito lokaḥ kaccit puruṣasattamaiḥ
english: Where are all those great warriors, valiant as tigers? Has this world been won by them too, those most excellent of men?

sanskrit: yadi lokān imān prāptās te ca sarve mahārathāḥ sthitaṃ vitta hi māṃ devāḥ sahitaṃ tair mahātmabhiḥ
english: If all those great warriors have attained these worlds, then know, O gods, that I shall abide here only in the company of those great-souled ones.

sanskrit: kaccin na tair avāpto 'yaṃ nṛpair loko 'kṣayaḥ śubhaḥ na tair ahaṃ vinā vatsye jñātibhir bhrātṛbhis tathā
english: Surely this imperishable, blessed world has been gained by those kings? Without them—my kinsmen and brothers—I will not dwell here.

sanskrit: mātur hi vacanaṃ śrutvā tadā salilakarmaṇi karṇasya kriyatāṃ toyam iti tapyāmi tena vai
english: For having heard my mother's words at the time of the water-rites—'Let the libation of water be made for Karṇa'—it is by that I am tormented even now.

sanskrit: idaṃ ca paritapyāmi punaḥ punar ahaṃ surāḥ yan mātuḥ sadṛśau pādau tasyāham amitaujasaḥ
english: And this too torments me again and again, O gods: that his feet were like my mother's, that man of measureless might.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvaiva taṃ nānugataḥ karṇaṃ parabalārdanam na hy asmān karṇasahitāñ jayec chakro 'pi saṃyuge
english: Yet even on seeing this I did not go over to Karṇa, the crusher of enemy hosts—for with Karṇa at our side not even Śakra could have vanquished us in battle.

sanskrit: tam ahaṃ yatratatrasthaṃ draṣṭum icchāmi sūryajam avijñāto mayā yo 'sau ghātitaḥ savyasācinā
english: Wherever he may be, I long to see him, the son of Sūrya—he who, unknown to me, was slain by Savyasācin.

sanskrit: bhīmaṃ ca bhīmavikrāntaṃ prāṇebhyo 'pi priyaṃ mama arjunaṃ cendrasaṃkāśaṃ yamau tau ca yamopamau
english: And Bhīma of terrible prowess, dearer to me than life itself; and Arjuna, like unto Indra; and those two twins, the equals of the Aśvins.

sanskrit: draṣṭum icchāmi tāṃ cāhaṃ pāñcālīṃ dharmacāriṇīm na ceha sthātum icchāmi satyam etad bravīmi vaḥ
english: And I wish to behold the Pāñcāla princess, devoted to righteousness. I do not wish to remain here—this truth I tell you.

sanskrit: kiṃ me bhrātṛvihīnasya svargeṇa surasattamāḥ yatra te sa mama svargo nāyaṃ svargo mato mama
english: What is heaven to me, bereft of my brothers, O best of the gods? Where they are, there is my heaven; this is no heaven in my eyes.

sanskrit: devā ūcuḥ yadi vai tatra te śraddhā gamyatāṃ putra māciram priye hi tava vartāmo devarājasya śāsanāt
english: The gods said: If your heart is set on going there, then go, my son, without delay; for we act to please you, by command of the king of the gods.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca ity uktvā taṃ tato devā devadūtam upādiśan yudhiṣṭhirasya suhṛdo darśayeti paraṃtapa
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having spoken thus to him, the gods then instructed a divine messenger: Show Yudhiṣṭhira his friends, O scorcher of foes.

sanskrit: tataḥ kuntīsuto rājā devadūtaś ca jagmatuḥ sahitau rājaśārdūla yatra te puruṣarṣabhāḥ
english: Then the king, the son of Kuntī, and the divine messenger went forth together, O tiger among kings, to where those bulls among men were.

sanskrit: agrato devadūtas tu yayau rājā ca pṛṣṭhataḥ panthānam aśubhaṃ durgaṃ sevitaṃ pāpakarmabhiḥ
english: The divine messenger went in front and the king behind, along a foul and difficult path frequented by evildoers.

sanskrit: tamasā saṃvṛtaṃ ghoraṃ keśaśaivalaśādvalam yuktaṃ pāpakṛtāṃ gandhair māṃsaśoṇitakardamam
english: shrouded in darkness, terrible, its grass and moss made of hair, reeking with the stench of those who had done evil, a mire of flesh and blood;

sanskrit: daṃśotthānaṃ sajhillīkaṃ makṣikāmaśakāvṛtam itaś cetaś ca kuṇapaiḥ samantāt parivāritam
english: swarming with gadflies and crickets, covered with flies and gnats, hemmed in on every side, here and there, with corpses;

sanskrit: asthikeśasamākīrṇaṃ kṛmikīṭasamākulam jvalanena pradīptena samantāt pariveṣṭitam
english: strewn with bones and hair, teeming with worms and insects, and on all sides girdled with blazing fire;

sanskrit: ayomukhaiś ca kākolair gṛdhraiś ca samabhidrutam sūcīmukhais tathā pretair vindhyaśailopamair vṛtam
english: overrun by iron-beaked ravens and vultures, and beset by needle-mouthed ghosts as huge as the Vindhya mountains;

sanskrit: medorudhirayuktaiś ca chinnabāhūrupāṇibhiḥ nikṛttodarapādaiś ca tatra tatra praveritaiḥ
english: and with severed arms, thighs, and hands smeared with marrow and blood, and bellies and feet cut off, flung about here and there.

sanskrit: sa tat kuṇapadurgandham aśivaṃ romaharṣaṇam jagāma rājā dharmātmā madhye bahu vicintayan
english: Through the midst of that corpse-stinking place, inauspicious and hair-raising, the righteous king passed, pondering much.

sanskrit: dadarśoṣṇodakaiḥ pūrṇāṃ nadīṃ cāpi sudurgamām asipatravanaṃ caiva niśitakṣurasaṃvṛtam
english: He saw a river filled with scalding water and hard to cross, and a forest whose leaves were swords, hedged about with sharp razors.

sanskrit: karambhavālukās taptā āyasīś ca śilāḥ pṛthak lohakumbhīś ca tailasya kvāthyamānāḥ samantataḥ
english: He saw burning sands of gravel, and slabs of iron set apart, and cauldrons of iron with oil seething on every side.

sanskrit: kūṭaśālmalikaṃ cāpi dusparśaṃ tīkṣṇakaṇṭakam dadarśa cāpi kaunteyo yātanāḥ pāpakarmiṇām
english: And the son of Kuntī beheld the thorny śālmali tree, untouchable with its sharp spikes, and the torments of those who had done evil.

sanskrit: sa taṃ durgandham ālakṣya devadūtam uvāca ha kiyad adhvānam asmābhir gantavyam idam īdṛśam
english: Marking that foul stench, he spoke to the divine messenger: How far must we travel along such a road as this?

sanskrit: kva ca te bhrātaro mahyaṃ tan mamākhyātum arhasi deśo 'yaṃ kaś ca devānām etad icchāmi veditum
english: And where are my brothers? This you ought to tell me. And what region of the gods is this? This I wish to know.

sanskrit: sa saṃnivavṛte śrutvā dharmarājasya bhāṣitam devadūto 'bravīc cainam etāvad gamanaṃ tava
english: Hearing the words of the Dharma-king, the divine messenger turned back and said to him: Thus far does your journey go.

sanskrit: nivartitavyaṃ hi mayā tathāsmy ukto divaukasaiḥ yadi śrānto 'si rājendra tvam athāgantum arhasi
english: For I must turn back, so I was told by the dwellers in heaven. If you are weary, O lord of kings, then you may return.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhiras tu nirviṇṇas tena gandhena mūrchitaḥ nivartane dhṛtamanāḥ paryāvartata bhārata
english: But Yudhiṣṭhira, sickened and faint from that stench, set his mind on returning and turned back, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: sa saṃnivṛtto dharmātmā duḥkhaśokasamanvitaḥ śuśrāva tatra vadatāṃ dīnā vācaḥ samantataḥ
english: As the righteous one turned back, filled with grief and sorrow, he heard piteous voices speaking all around him there.

sanskrit: bho bho dharmaja rājarṣe puṇyābhijana pāṇḍava anugrahārtham asmākaṃ tiṣṭha tāvan muhūrtakam
english: O son of Dharma, royal sage, Pāṇḍava of holy lineage! For our sake, in mercy, stay but a moment longer.

sanskrit: āyāti tvayi durdharṣe vāti puṇyaḥ samīraṇaḥ tava gandhānugas tāta yenāsmān sukham āgamat
english: As you, unassailable one, draw near, a holy breeze blows, bearing your fragrance, dear lord, by which ease has come to us.

sanskrit: te vayaṃ pārtha dīrghasya kālasya puruṣarṣabha sukham āsādayiṣyāmas tvāṃ dṛṣṭvā rājasattama
english: We, O Pārtha, bull among men, after so long a time shall find relief at the sight of you, O best of kings.

sanskrit: saṃtiṣṭhasva mahābāho muhūrtam api bhārata tvayi tiṣṭhati kauravya yātanāsmān na bādhate
english: Stay, mighty-armed one, even for a moment, O Bhārata; for while you remain, O Kaurava, the torment does not afflict us.

sanskrit: evaṃ bahuvidhā vācaḥ kṛpaṇā vedanāvatām tasmin deśe sa śuśrāva samantād vadatāṃ nṛpa
english: Such manifold pitiful voices of those in agony did he hear, O king, as they cried out on every side in that place.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ tad vacanaṃ śrutvā dayāvān dīnabhāṣiṇām aho kṛcchram iti prāha tasthau sa ca yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: Hearing those words of the wretched speakers, the compassionate Yudhiṣṭhira cried, Alas, what misery! and halted where he stood.

sanskrit: sa tā giraḥ purastād vai śrutapūrvāḥ punaḥ punaḥ glānānāṃ duḥkhitānāṃ ca nābhyajānata pāṇḍavaḥ
english: Those voices of the faint and the suffering, heard before now again and again, the Pāṇḍava could not recognize.

sanskrit: abudhyamānas tā vāco dharmaputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ uvāca ke bhavanto vai kimartham iha tiṣṭhatha
english: Not understanding those voices, Yudhiṣṭhira, the son of Dharma, said: Who are you, and why do you remain here?

sanskrit: ity uktās te tataḥ sarve samantād avabhāṣire karṇo 'haṃ bhīmaseno 'ham arjuno 'ham iti prabho
english: Thus addressed, they all then cried out from every side: I am Karṇa, I am Bhīmasena, I am Arjuna, O lord!

sanskrit: nakulaḥ sahadevo 'haṃ dhṛṣṭadyumno 'ham ity uta draupadī draupadeyāś ca ity evaṃ te vicukruśuḥ
english: I am Nakula, I am Sahadeva, I am Dhṛṣṭadyumna; I am Draupadī, and we are the sons of Draupadī—thus they cried aloud.

sanskrit: tā vācaḥ sā tadā śrutvā taddeśasadṛśīr nṛpa tato vimamṛśe rājā kiṃ nv idaṃ daivakāritam
english: Hearing those voices, fitting to that place, O king, the king then reflected: What is this, brought about by fate?

sanskrit: kiṃ nu tat kaluṣaṃ karma kṛtam ebhir mahātmabhiḥ karṇena draupadeyair vā pāñcālyā vā sumadhyayā
english: What sinful deed can have been done by these great-souled ones—by Karṇa, or by the sons of Draupadī, or by the fair-waisted Pāñcāla princess—

sanskrit: ya ime pāpagandhe 'smin deśe santi sudāruṇe na hi jānāmi sarveṣāṃ duṣkṛtaṃ puṇyakarmaṇām
english: that they should be in this dreadful, evil-smelling region? For I know of no misdeed in all these doers of holy works.

sanskrit: kiṃ kṛtvā dhṛtarāṣṭrasya putro rājā suyodhanaḥ tathā śriyā yutaḥ pāpaḥ saha sarvaiḥ padānugaiḥ
english: What has the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra done, King Suyodhana, the wicked one, that he should be endowed with such splendor, together with all his followers,

sanskrit: mahendra iva lakṣmīvān āste paramapūjitaḥ kasyedānīṃ vikāro 'yaṃ yad ime narakaṃ gatāḥ
english: and sit there glorious as great Indra, supremely honored? Whose doing now is this perversion, that these have gone to hell?

sanskrit: sarvadharmavidaḥ śūrāḥ satyāgamaparāyaṇāḥ kṣātradharmaparāḥ prājñā yajvāno bhūridakṣiṇāḥ
english: They who knew every law, brave men devoted to truth and scripture, intent on the warrior's duty, wise, performers of sacrifice with abundant gifts—

sanskrit: kiṃ nu supto 'smi jāgarmi cetayāno na cetaye aho cittavikāro 'yaṃ syād vā me cittavibhramaḥ
english: Am I asleep or awake? I am conscious, yet I do not comprehend. Ah, this must be some disorder of my mind, or some delusion of my senses.

sanskrit: evaṃ bahuvidhaṃ rājā vimamarśa yudhiṣṭhiraḥ duḥkhaśokasamāviṣṭaś cintāvyākulitendriyaḥ
english: In such manifold ways did King Yudhiṣṭhira reflect, overcome with grief and sorrow, his senses confounded by anguished thought.

sanskrit: krodham āhārayac caiva tīvraṃ dharmasuto nṛpaḥ devāṃś ca garhayām āsa dharmaṃ caiva yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: And King Yudhiṣṭhira, the son of Dharma, gave way to fierce anger, and reproached both the gods and Dharma himself.

sanskrit: sa tīvragandhasaṃtapto devadūtam uvāca ha gamyatāṃ bhadra yeṣāṃ tvaṃ dūtas teṣām upāntikam
english: Tormented by that pungent stench, he said to the divine messenger: Go, good sir, into the presence of those whose messenger you are.

sanskrit: na hy ahaṃ tatra yāsmyāmi sthito 'smīti nivedyatām matsaṃśrayād ime dūta sukhino bhrātaro hi me
english: For I shall not go there; let it be made known that I remain here. For through my presence, O messenger, these my brothers find ease.

sanskrit: ity uktaḥ sa tadā dūtaḥ pāṇḍuputreṇa dhīmatā jagāma tatra yatrāste devarājaḥ śatakratuḥ
english: Thus addressed by the wise son of Pāṇḍu, the messenger then went to where the king of the gods, Śatakratu, abode.

sanskrit: nivedayām āsa ca tad dharmarājacikīrṣitam yathoktaṃ dharmaputreṇa sarvam eva janādhipa
english: And he reported the Dharma-king's resolve, all of it just as the son of Dharma had spoken it, O lord of men.
